name: The men at Lee's Place on the South Branch
head: white_liberty

present_on_scene_date.note: Dead or gone before 14 August 1812; in the town on the earlier dates their cards give.

associated_with.note: Lee's farm, where Liberty White had charge and he and Cardin were killed on 6 April 1812 (Quaife ch. X).

not_in_this_household.note: Everyone the T-3463..T-3467 day readings put in this household is on the card (liberty L-1812-town-days-3463).

persons.name: Liberty White

present_on_scene_date.note: Dead on 6 April 1812. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: An American who had charge of Lee's farm on the South Branch, killed there on 6 April 1812. In the town from 1811-01-01 to 1812-04-06: He "had lived at Chicago for some time" (Quaife, from Kinzie's account books; the start is ours). Killed at Lee's Place a little before sunset on 6 April 1812 (Heald; Wau-Bun the 7th).

evidence.quote: The farm was under the immediate superintendence of an American named Liberty White, who had lived at Chicago for some time.
evidence.claim: an American in charge of the farm

evidence.locator: p. 43 (Heald, 15 April 1812), data/research/books/text/moses_kirkland_history_of_chicago_v1.txt lines 6884-6887 (machine OCR, read as corrected)
evidence.quote: where they murdered two men, one by the name of Liberty White, an American

evidence.locator: ch. XVIII, PG 51737 (1856 text as reprinted in the 1901 Caxton Club edition) lines 5775-5776
evidence.quote: The body of Mr. White was found pierced by two balls, and with eleven stabs in the breast.

persons.name: Jean Baptiste Cardin (Debou in Currey)

present_on_scene_date.note: Dead on 6 April 1812. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: A Canadian newly come to Chicago (Currey calls him Debou), killed with Liberty White at Lee's Place on 6 April 1812. In the town from 1812-03-01 to 1812-04-06: A Canadian "who had but recently come to Chicago" (Quaife): the start is ours. Killed with White on 6 April 1812.

evidence.quote: a Canadian Frenchman, John B. Cardin, who had but recently come to Chicago

evidence.locator: ch. XVIII, PG 51737 (1856 text as reprinted in the 1901 Caxton Club edition) lines 5706-5707
evidence.quote: I know by their dress and paint that they are not Pottowattamies.
